Here’s everything you need to know about the saga that has erupted this week and the very famous name circulated as the possible successor to the (for now) current USMNT manager, Mauricio Pochettino. Who Is Pep Guardiola? Basically, Guardiola is the world’s gold standard for soccer management at the international club level, but someone whose experience has come primarily from coaching the world’s biggest stars. The best North American parallels might be pro baseball’s Tony La Russa, pro basketball’s Phil Jackson, college basketball’s Rick Pitino or college football’s Nick Saban. In other words, guys who have achieved the highest heights at multiple stops. Guardiola has won prolifically at three stops; FC Barcelona, Bayern Munich and most recently Manchester City. In total, the Spaniard owns 12 league titles, three UEFA Champions League crowns and four FIFA Club World Cups (in the now-defunct annual format). Why Does The USMNT Need A New Manager? Essentially, it looks like Mauricio Pochettino is leaving to take over at Manchester United. Pochettino signed a four-year extension with U.S. Soccer to stay with the USMNT in August. But such is his stature that his name is often bandied about when a high-profile English or European job comes open. This time the rumors have real legs, though. ESPN’s Mark Ogden first reported Manchester United preferred Pochettino as a candidate to replace current manager Michael Carrick , and the Guardian’s Pablo Maurer and Jamie Jackson first confirmed the interest was mutual . Additional reports have negotiations progressing. The good news for U.S. fans is it appears U.S. Soccer will be compensated should Pochettino leave, with a $10 million buyout clause reportedly a part of his new contract. top.title: Mizzou volleyball adds three-player class on National Signing Day
top.description: Dawn Sullivan’s 2027 recruiting class features a nationally recognized setter, an accomplished defensive specialist and a St. Louis middle blocker. Mizzou announced the signings of Lucky Fasavalu, Dani Lewis and Marlee Steiner on Wednesday, adding three players who bring experience at the national, state and club levels. The group addresses three different positions for Sullivan’s program, with Fasavalu expected to help direct the offense, Lewis strengthening the back row and Steiner providing another option at the net. Fasavalu, a 5-foot-8 setter from Sierra Canyon High School in California, arrives in Columbia with an extensive list of individual accomplishments. She was named a MaxPreps First Team All-American in 2025 and earned recognition on the organization’s National Player of the Year watchlist. Fasavalu recently reached another milestone, recording her 2,000th career assist during Sierra Canyon’s postseason run. The Trailblazers advanced to the CIF Southern Section Division I championship match Nov. 7, finishing as runner-up to Mater Dei. Lewis, a 5-foot-5 defensive specialist from Lake Norman Charter in North Carolina, joins the Tigers after winning back-to-back state championships. The libero was named the most valuable player of North Carolina’s 4A state competition during the latest championship run. She also earned Charlotte-area Player of the Year recognition from the Charlotte Observer and played club volleyball with Carolina Union. Lewis served as a team captain at Lake Norman Charter, which finished the 2026 season with a 30-1 record. Steiner gives Missouri another in-state addition. The 6-foot-5 middle blocker from Lindbergh High School in St. Louis has experience competing with USA Volleyball’s national development programs and was selected to the U19 National Team roster. She also played club volleyball with High Performance STL. Steiner earned First Team All-State recognition in Missouri in 2025 and was named to the JVA All-National Team in each of the past two seasons. The three signings give Sullivan another recruiting group as Missouri continues building its roster for the future. With a setter who has surpassed 2,000 career assists, a defensive specialist with championship experience and a 6-foot-5 middle blocker, the Tigers bring in players with different skill sets and competitive backgrounds. Fasavalu, Lewis and Steiner are expected to join Missouri for the 2027 season.

top.description: Oregon's Dan Lanning calls out Michigan football for bad spending habits originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Oregon Ducks coach Dan Lanning took a slight shot at Michigan for how the football program has distributed its money. This came in response to comments about the Ducks' financial advantages in recruiting and roster building. The exchange began when Michigan Wolverines coach Kyle Whittingham suggested Oregon's reported $50 million budget gave the program a significant advantage in the increasingly competitive NIL landscape. Whittingham praised Lanning for his work, but also acknowledged the resources available to Oregon, mostly tied to Nike. "It doesn't hurt that you have $50-plus million dollars at your disposal to, in essence, outbid everybody,' Whittingham said. "Not everybody, but a lot of people." Lanning took issue with the basis of the comment. He responded by talking about Michigan's financial commitments, particularly money still owed to departing coaches. "They're spending more of their money right now on their coaches that they're letting go, so maybe it makes it hard to sign players,'" Lanning said. He also suggested Michigan had secured players Oregon could not match financially. "I know they've signed a couple of guys that we weren't able to compete with what they decided to do,' Lanning said. "Maybe a lot of that money is tied up for them in another player." Dan Lanning’s response to Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham’s comments on Oregon being able to “outbid everybody” for recruits. pic.twitter.com/zsVwvrppUc — Ryan Clarke (@RyanTClarke) November 11, 2026 The comments add another storyline ahead of Michigan's trip to Eugene this week. Lanning and Whittingham know each other extremely well, being in the Pac-12 for their respective schools. Whittingham made the transition to Ann Arbor from Utah over the offseason. According to On3, Oregon quarterback Dante Moore carries a $5 million NIL valuation, ranking fourth nationally. EDGE Matayo Uiagalelei and safety Koi Perich also appear in the top 100, each valued at $2 million. Michigan has two players on the list. Quarterback Bryce Underwood carries a $3 million valuation, ranking 33rd. But in reality, his NIL deal with the school was a reported $12.5 million. EDGE John Henry Daley is valued at $2 million after coming over from Utah. Despite the back-and-forth, Lanning made it clear he respects Whittingham, calling him an unbelievable Hall of Fame-caliber coach. Both programs compete for top talent. However, this year hasn't been typical for either the Wolverines or Ducks. No. 18 Oregon hosts Michigan on Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET on FS1. top.title: Jacob Misiorowski wins unanimous NL Cy Young Award; Cam Schlittler claims AL honors
top.description: ST PETERSBURG, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 28: Jacob Misiorowski #32 of the Milwaukee Brewers reacts during the fifth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game five of the 2026 World Series at Tropicana Field on October 28, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the third year in a row, the Cy Young race was somewhat of a foregone conclusion. Today, Brewers right-hander Jacob Misiorowski was named the unanimous National League Cy Young Award winner, joining Randy Johnson (2001) and Justin Verlander (2022) as the only pitchers since 2000 to win the Cy Young and the World Series in the same year. He is the fourth Brewer to win the award in franchise history, following Rollie Fingers (1981), Pete Vuckovich (1982), and Corbin Burnes (2021). Misiorowski flashed as a rookie last year, starting off hot and (controversially) making the All-Star team after just five career starts, but he struggled with his command down the stretch and finished the year with a 4.36 ERA. This year, in his first full season as a big-leaguer, Misiorowski worked out the kinks and became completely and utterly dominant, leading the majors in ERA (1.80), strikeouts (252), and WHIP (0.80) while going 16-5. Highlights from his record-breaking season include: Making history with the first-ever 15-strikeout “Maddux” (a complete-game shutout on fewer than 100 pitches) in an early-June game against the Phillies. Misiorowski was a Kyle Schwarber single away from a perfect game, and his 15 strikeouts tied Corbin Burnes for the second-most in a game in Brewers history, behind only Ben Sheets (18). Setting the record for the fastest pitch ever thrown by a starting pitcher, a 105.5-mph fastball. Throwing 1,115 pitches at 100 mph or harder, the most in a season since tracking began in 2008, shattering Jordan Hicks’ previous record of 673 in 2018. Making the National League All-Star team for the second time in as many years. Holding opponents to a .157 batting average, the lowest on record for a full season. Becoming the first Brewer in history to lead the league in both ERA and strikeouts in the same season. Starting the game that clinched the first World Series title in franchise history. Cristopher Sánchez of the Phillies finished second for the second year in a row, receiving 17 of 30 second-place votes, while Braves left-hander Chris Sale finished third. In the American League, fellow second-year starter Cam Schlittler also won the award unanimously. Schlittler put together an amazing season of his own, leading AL starters in WAR (7.0), ERA (1.95), and ERA+ (215). Dylan Cease of the Blue Jays finished second, and rookie Parker Messick of the Guardians finished third.

top.description: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - MARCH 16: Alex Vesia (L) #51 and Tanner Scott #66 of the Los Angeles Dodgers walk on the field prior to a Spring Training game against the Milwaukee Brewers at Camelback Ranch on March 16, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. The inaugural winner of the National League Reliever of the Year is Mason Miller in a landslide. The San Diego Padres closer received all 30 first-place votes. His stats tell the story, as Miller put up a 1.67 ERA, best among all National League pitchers with 50 innings. Miller was also tops in xERA (1.70), FIP (1.17), xFIP (1.54), strikeout rate (an eye-popping 47.4 percent), strikeout-minus-walk rate (37.9 percent), and saves (38, in 41 attempts). I had a vote in this award this year, and I voted Miller in the top spot. Before casting my ballot, I asked a few Dodgers relievers how they might define relief pitcher of the year, and in the course of our conversations, Miller also gained their respect, too. “It’s got to be Mason Miller,” said left-hander Alex Veisa. “He has been unbelievable to watch. His stuff is — you know, when he was in Oakland, right, it’s like how could someone get any better? I was not only certain pretty early on about Miller in the top spot, but also Johan Duran of the Philadelphia Phillies seemed like the clear choice for my No. 2 on the ballot. top.title: Eduardo Rodriguez 7th in NL Cy Young voting
top.description: MIAMI, FLORIDA - APRIL 17: Eduardo Rodriguez #57 of the Arizona Diamondbacks looks on following the first inning against the Miami Marlins at loanDepot park on April 17, 2025 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images Unsurprisingly, Jacob Misiorowski was the winner of the NL Cy Young award, getting all thirty first-place votes. But there was some love for Arizona further down the ballot, with Eduardo Rodriguez getting two fifth-place votes, from Tyler Kepner of the Athletic, and Dejan Kovacevic of DK Pittsburgh Sports. E-Rod is the first D-back to be mentioned since 2023, and the first apart from Zac Gallen since 2018. Here are the Diamondbacks to receive votes in the NL Cy Young balloting over the past twenty years, since Brandon Webb was the last Diamondback to take home the award. 2026: Eduardo Rodriguez – 7th, 2 points 2023: Zac Gallen – 3rd, 68 points 2022: Zac Gallen – 5th, 45 points 2020: Zac Gallen – =9th, 2 points 2018: Patrick Corbin – 5th, 23 points 2017: Zack Greinke – 4th, 52 points + Robbie Ray – 7th, 6 points 2011: Ian Kennedy – 4th, 76 points 2009: Dan Haren – 5th, 1 point 2008: Brandon Webb – 2nd, 76 points 2007: Brandon Webb – 2nd, 94 points + Jose Valverde – =6th, 2 points 2006: Brandon Webb – 1st, 106 points This year feels like a Rorschach Test for how the BBWAA evaluate pitchers. Rodriguez did considerably better in the old school metrics. His ERA of 2.89 was fifth among qualified pitchers in the National League, and by wins (16), he only trailed Cristopher Sánchez of the Phillies (18). Innings pitched also had E-Rod ranked highly, third in the NL. [Though in a sign of the times, only two pitchers reached even 190 innings. As recently as 2014, twenty-seven pitchers in the NL did] But Rodriguez ranked only seventh by bWAR among pitchers (4.7), and fWAR ranked him all the way down at 12th, on 3.2 wins, likely due to his FIP being a run more than his ERA. In the old-school era – like when Brandon Webb lost out on Rookie of the Year in 2003 to Dontrelle Willis, I suspect Eduardo would perhaps have made the top three. But W’s and, to a lesser extent, ERA are no longer seen as the definitive measure of pitcher quality. I’m somewhat torn about that. Wins, I get. While good starters will tend to pick up more of them, the offense plays a huge part in that, and is something over which the pitcher has no control. ERA is also dependent on external factors, albeit to a lesser extent, with defense a factor, beyond what is recorded in earned vs. unearned runs. But generating weak contact, leading to “better” defense, feels like a skill too. Still, there’s no denying Rodriguez had an excellent, and much-needed, season for Arizona. top.title: Youngest pair of Cy Young winners in 41 years shows future of pitching has arrived
top.description: They embraced the modern ethos of pitching from the moment they turned professional. And now Jacob Misiorowski and Cam Schlittler have proven the future of pitching has arrived. Misiorowski, 24, and Schlittler, 25, won the National and American league Cy Young Awards , respectively, in balloting announced on Nov. 11. And in doing so, they made a certain kind of history: They are the youngest Cy Young-winning duo since 1985, when 20-year-old Dwight Gooden and 21-year-old Bret Saberhagen took home NL and AL honors. Gooden and Saberhagen went on to excellent, World Series-winning careers, even if they could not sustain that level of dominance when they were barely or not quite old enough to legally drink. And their victories didn’t necessarily portend a changing of the guard in the pitching pantheon. Yet, The Miz and Schlitt seemed to prove a point in making 30 and 33 starts and consistently pitching deep into games for the Milwaukee Brewers and New York Yankees , respectively: Yes, significant gains in velocity can be taught – and throwing as hard as you can as long as you can, at least for one season, is sustainable. Schlittler’s fastball barely hit 88 mph coming out of Northeastern as a seventh-round pick in 2022. Misiorowski was in that same range when Brewers scouts pondered drafting him out of high school. Yet both young men matured physically. Schlittler now packs 215 pounds on his 6-foot-6 frame, while Misiorowski is still a relative drink of water at 6-7, 201 – but seemingly growing every day. Perhaps more important, they got drafted by clubs that were fantastic fits. Schlittler’s mechanics and repertoire were remade under a pitching department led by Sam Briend, a former Driveline director of pitching and now the senior voice among Yankee pitching staffers. One of Briend’s first hires, Preston Claiborne, came up the ladder with Schlittler and is now assistant pitching coach for the major league club. Meanwhile, Misiorowski has exceeded the hopes Brewers scouts held when they projected he’d eventually top 100 mph. Try 105 mph. The Miz threw 28 of the 35 hardest pitches in the major leagues this season, ranging from 104 to 105.5 mph. That’s great eye candy, but the numbers at the end of September are even better: 252 strikeouts with a 1.80 ERA, two of the seven major statistical categories in which Misiorowski led the major leagues. Schlittler won his own ERA title, posting a 1.95 mark to lead the AL. And he pitched 193 2/3 innings, just shy of the 200-inning plateau that was once the bare minimum of quality production, yet just three pitchers exceeded this season. Still, for Schlittler to reach that mark in his first full season is an excellent sign he might yet resemble what we all considered an ace. top.description: MOUNT OLIVE — Ava Diaz held the NJSIAA Group 3 North volleyball trophy tightly, with both arms. Amidst the chaotic back gym, the Mount Olive senior libero looked back on the season – and a chance to make history. The Marauders held off North Hunterdon, 25-18, 25-23, 25-23, to clinch the sectional title and extend a confusing and challenging season. Diaz played libero for Mount Olive for the first time, just her second year at the defensive spot. But the big change impacted outside hitters Izabella Osoria and Olivia Drucks. Instead of just stepping up at the net, both became setters – usually to each other. What head coach "modified 6-2" was the brainchild of assistant coach Lee Clowers back in preseason. It took a little while to adjust – noted in the Marauders' lone loss at Randolph on Sept. 9 – but it's become their not-so-secret weapon. Mount Olive won the NJAC-American for the third straight year, knocked off Randolph in the Morris County Tournament final, and now will make its first trip to the Group final since 2016. The Marauders will play Group 3 South champion Toms River South at 1 p.m. Nov. 14 at Franklin High School. Flashback! Mount Olive's big hitters pave path to MCT volleyball title "This was my final time to prove how good of a team we are," said Diaz, who had 33 digs, a kill, two assists and two aces. "This team, specifically, we have a ton of fire in us. We're all like a family. That's what drives us." With her grandmother, parents, and aunt Elizabeth Vega from Orlando, Florida, watching from the front row of the bleachers, Osoria had 16 kills, 14 digs, 22 assists and an ace in the sectional final. Drucks added a team-high 20 kills, three blocks, four digs and 15 assists. "It's normal to have a setter. Every high school has that setter. It's a creative idea," said Drucks, a sophomore who has never set before. "It feels really good it was able to work out. At first I was questionable. 'Can I set well enough?' People say it's odd, but it works, so why not?" This article originally appeared on Morristown Daily Record: Mount Olive volleyball tops North Hunterdon, advances to Group final

David Morgan Morgan went undrafted in 2022 but was invited to a workout with other prospects at Petco Park. In 47 1/3 innings of work, the right-hander quickly became a high-leverage option for San Diego down the stretch, authoring a 2.66 ERA in that time. Overall Grade: C Last season was a step back from that dominant rookie campaign. Morgan posted a 3.78 ERA, 1.77 WHIP and .282 opponent batting average across 33 1/3 innings. nigeria.description: Last week, I started a discussion of General Yakubu Gowon’s multi-themed memoirs, My Life of Duty & Allegiance. My focus was on the book’s general tone, which I find unduly self-justificatory. In his attempts to defend his legacy, General Gowon presents himself as a saintly figure who did no wrong as a leader, whereas some introspection and nuanced reflection would have helped. That said, the book is a treasure trove of insightful details that enrich our historical narrative. This week, I will focus on one of such insights, namely, the quality of governance and public service ethos under General Gowon’s regime, with Chief Obafemi Awolowo singled out as the arrowhead of a remarkable governance approach that, if replicated today, would transform how Nigeria is governed and, thus, this country’s fortunes. As a political economist and policy practitioner who spent nearly 20 years advising the UK government on diverse policy areas, in addition to teaching public policy, I have professional and intellectual interests in how government is run. Thus, I was enthralled by General Gowon’s fascinating accounts of how the affairs of state were conducted under his administration, with the triumvirate of politicians (as ministers), civil servants (as technocrats), and universities and think-tanks (as sounding boards) driving policy formulation and implementation and setting standards of good and effective governance. Sitting atop the triumvirate was Chief Awolowo, an extraordinarily transformative leader! Indeed, if General Gowon’s memoirs can be said to have a hero, that hero is Chief Obafemi Awolowo, appointed by Gowon as the Vice Chairman of the Federal Executive Council, FEC, and Commissioner of Finance in his administration. nigeria.title: The US built world’s greatest card system
nigeria.description: By YVONNE-FAITH ELAIGWU The history of payments is, in many ways, the history of making value easier to move. We started at barter and are now at electronic transfers, with stablecoins suggesting that the next evolution is here. New payment methods rarely make their predecessors useless. Cash did not immediately eliminate barter. Cards did not eliminate cheques. Account-to-account payments will not eliminate cards. But payments evolve. And one of the most interesting examples of that evolution can be found in an unlikely comparison: Nigeria and the United States. The United States built perhaps the world’s greatest card ecosystem. Nigeria just seems to have built past it. The American card system is extraordinary. Over decades, the U.S. built an ecosystem connecting consumers, merchants, issuing banks, acquiring banks, and card networks. Around it grew credit bureaus, credit scores, revolving credit, chargebacks, fraud protection, loyalty points, airline miles, and billions of dollars of rewards. Consequently, Americans have a compelling reason to use cards. And use them, they do. Data from the Federal Reserve show that credit-card payments reached 67.1 billion transactions in 2024, while ACH processed an enormous $104.06 trillion in 2024. America, therefore, doesn’t lack account-to-account infrastructure. The difference is where A2A sits in everyday consumer behaviour. Walk into an American store, and the natural question is still: Which card am I using? In Nigeria, increasingly, a different question is asked: “What is your account number?” That difference is more significant than it appears. Nigeria took another road. Nigeria never developed America’s deep credit-card culture. Debit cards became widespread, but cards did not become as deeply embedded in the country’s economic architecture as they did in America. Instead, Nigeria increasingly solved digital payments at the bank-account level. At the centre of this transformation is the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System and its NIBSS Instant Payment platform, built to operate 24/7 with most transactions settling in under one second. This infrastructure changed behaviour. Any individual or company can pay another individual or merchant, and the transaction can be executed on a Friday evening or a Sunday morning. The expectation is still remarkably simple: the money should arrive now. That expectation is one of Nigeria’s greatest payment achievements. America’s success may be part of its problem. This is where the comparison becomes fascinating. America isn’t stuck on cards because it cannot build something better. It may be stuck on cards partly because cards work so well. The merchant already has the terminal. The consumer already has the card. The bank earns card revenue. Visa and Mastercard provide enormous networks. nigeria.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri With the 2027 general elections just 65 days away, all eyes are on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to conduct a smooth, free, fair, and credible poll. Meanwhile, preparations for the aftermath are already under way. A total of 375 judges have been nominated to serve on election petition tribunals, where they will adjudicate disputes brought by candidates and parties dissatisfied with the results. The judges, drawn from courts across the federation, were inaugurated on Monday, November 9, at a ceremony held at the Body of Benchers Complex in Abuja. Section 285(1) and (2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, vests in the President of the Court of Appeal the responsibility for constituting election petition tribunals to adjudicate disputes arising from National and State Houses of Assembly and governorship elections. Similarly, section 134(3)(a) and (b) of the Electoral Act, 2026, prescribes the timelines for constituting the tribunals and opening their registries. The swearing-in, organised by the President of the Court of Appeal, Justice Monica Dongban-Mensem, marked the formal assumption of a responsibility with considerable constitutional, professional and public significance. A three-day intensive workshop followed immediately. It was designed to deepen the judges’ knowledge of the Electoral Act 2026, familiarise them with applicable practice directions and the evolving jurisprudence of the courts on election-related cases, and sharpen the practical skills needed for case management, evaluation of evidence, control of proceedings, and the delivery of clear, well-reasoned judgments within the prescribed timelines. The CJN also used the occasion to launch the second edition of the Judicial Electoral Manual (JEM), which she said will help judicial officers locate relevant authorities, appreciate the development of the law and approach recurring issues with greater clarity. According to the CJN, by bringing together the relevant constitutional provisions, the Electoral Act 2026, applicable practice directions and judicial decisions, the Manual provides a useful resource for judicial officers and other stakeholders in the electoral adjudicatory process. She was quick to warn, however, that it should serve only as a guide and a reference tool. It does not replace independent judicial reasoning or relieve any judicial officer of the duty to consider each case on its own facts, the arguments of counsel and the applicable law. nigeria.title: Gbenga Omotoso at 65: A rare gift of generosity and mentorship
nigeria.description: By ROBERT UWEMEDIMO When Debbi Fields observed that “there is no such thing as coincidence; people come into our lives for a reason,” she captured a truth I have come to know profoundly through my relationship with Mr. Gbenga Omotoso. As he turned 65 on November 11, 2026, I pause to reflect on the extraordinary journey of more than two decades I have been privileged to share with the man I call boss – one who has been to me a father, mentor, benefactor, teacher, and, above all, a blessing from God Almighty. April 21, 2004, marked the beginning of a journey that would forever alter the course of my life. As I approached the wine-coloured plywood door on the second floor of a six-storey building at Ijora Causeway, Lagos – then the headquarters of The Comet newspaper – I opened it and found myself face to face with Mr. Omotoso, the Daily Editor, who needed someone to run errands for his office. He asked my name. “Robert,” I replied. “When will you resume work?” he asked. I was stunned. Here stood a man offering me a job before I had even applied; no interview, no credentials to present, no long queue outside a human resources office. Just one simple question that would rewrite the course of my life. “Tomorrow, sir,” I answered. That brief exchange marked the beginning of a relationship that shaped my life in ways I could never have imagined. I was a young boy who had lost his father at twelve. Little did I know that God was preparing another father figure for me in the person of Mr. Omotoso. When The Comet closed in 2006, a deep and overwhelming sense of uncertainty settled over us. Yet Mr. Omotoso looked me in the eye and assured me that wherever his career took him next, I would not be left behind. True to his word, when The Nation newspaper launched on July 31, 2006, I continued working with him as a 16-year-old boy. One quality that set him apart from the very beginning was his uncommon, almost instinctive generosity. I remember one particular week when he repeatedly asked whether I had eaten. Each time, he would give me some money for food. nigeria.title: Right-sizing the map of Africa
nigeria.description: The United Nations General Assembly has, for the first time, formally endorsed a global shift away from the centuries-old Mercator map in favour of projections that show Africa—and other equatorial regions—in their true relative size. This “Correct the Map” resolution, spearheaded by Togo on behalf of the African Group and backed by the African Union, passed by 164 votes to one, with six abstentions. While non-binding, it marks a watershed moment in how the world visually represents the continent—and, by extension, how it perceives Africa’s weight in global affairs. The root of the misrepresentation lies in the Mercator projection, devised in 1569 by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator for maritime navigation. To keep compass bearings straight, Mercator preserved angles and shapes—but at the cost of area. The result: landmasses near the poles, such as Europe, North America and Greenland, are visually enlarged, while those near the equator, including Africa, Latin America and South Asia, are shrunk. On typical Mercator wall maps, Greenland appears roughly the same size as Africa. In reality, Africa covers about 30.3 million square kilometres, making it around 14 times larger than Greenland’s 2.1 million square kilometres. This is not a minor quirk; it is a systematic visual bias baked into the most widely used world map for nearly five centuries. The resolution encourages governments, schools, international organisations, media houses and technology companies to adopt equal-area projections, especially the Equal Earth projection, whenever comparative continental size matters. It frames map distortion as more than a technical issue—calling it a cognitive, educational, cultural and geopolitical problem that has contributed to the symbolic minimisation of Africa in the global imagination. While symbolic correction matters, Africa’s greatest vulnerabilities lie in structural exploitation and escalating insecurity, notably from Islamist insurgencies across the Sahel, Lake Chad Basin and parts of the Horn. Map reform must be paired with hard-edged action on multiple fronts. First, curb external exploitation and illicit financial flows by tightening transparency on extractives, choking illicit financial flows through cross-border tax cooperation, and rebalancing investment terms to prioritise local content and value addition. Third, lock in development dividends that undercut recruitment by expanding vocational training and agro-processing corridors tied to the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), funding climate-resilient livelihoods, and prioritising children’s education and primary healthcare. nigeria.description: The Canada government has announced plans to accelerate permanent residence (PR) processing for up to 200,000 foreign nationals already living in the country in 2027, as part of efforts to reduce immigration application backlogs and provide greater certainty for newcomers. The initiative, announced by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) under the 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan, will provide additional admissions spaces for selected workers and humanitarian applicants seeking to transition to permanent residence. According to the government, the measure will be implemented through two major groups: a workers’ cohort and a humanitarian cohort, with up to 100,000 spaces allocated to each. The workers’ category will cover eligible foreign workers already living in Canada, alongside their accompanying family members. The government intends to work with provincial and territorial authorities to identify workers who meet regional labour market requirements. Eligible workers will include those who qualify for permanent residence through the Provincial Nominee Program (PNP), as well as applicants awaiting decisions under selected federal immigration programmes. These programmes include the Atlantic Immigration Program, Start-Up Visa Program, Self-Employed Persons Program, Agri-Food Pilot and Home Care Worker programmes. The humanitarian category, also allocated up to 100,000 spaces, will cover people already in Canada who have been waiting for permanent residence decisions, including applicants under specific family reunification and humanitarian pathways. Among those expected to benefit from the humanitarian allocation are: Spouses, common-law partners and dependent children: Family members of Canadian citizens and permanent residents who have already applied for permanent residence and are awaiting final decisions. Hong Kong residents: Applicants under Canada’s permanent residence pathways for Hong Kong residents, which closed to new applications on August 31, 2026. Ukrainian nationals: Applicants under the Ukraine Family Reunification Pathway, which closed to new applications on October 22, 2024. Humanitarian and compassionate applicants: Individuals already in Canada whose applications for permanent residence have received approval in principle. The government said the additional spaces would help it process all remaining applications under the Hong Kong and Ukraine pathways, while also supporting family reunification and fulfilling existing humanitarian commitments. IRCC also said the initiative would help reduce waiting periods for spouses and partners of Canadian citizens and permanent residents, with the aim of bringing processing times closer to 12 months for applicants destined for provinces outside Quebec. nigeria.title: US withdraws from U17 World Cup in Qatar over security fears
nigeria.description: The United States has withdrawn from the upcoming Under-17 soccer World Cup in Qatar due to concerns about security in the Middle East, US media reported Wednesday. Players were informed of the decision just over a week before the tournament is due to begin on November 19, US Soccer Collective and The Athletic reported, citing anonymous sources. US Soccer, the sport’s governing body in the United States, did not immediately confirm the news or respond to AFP’s request for comment. The war in the Middle East began in February with joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran, which retaliated by targeting, among others, Gulf countries allied with Washington. Diplomatic efforts to end the conflict have been punctuated by repeated threats from the United States and Israel to resume bombardments of Iran. Multiple sporting events in the Middle East have been affected, including the tennis WTA Finals which were scheduled to be held in Saudi Arabia — which neighbors Qatar — but are instead now taking place at Indian Wells in the US. This season’s Formula One Grand Prix in Jeddah was cancelled, while the race in Bahrain was called off and later rescheduled under the same name in Malaysia. Several events in Saudi Arabia have also been cancelled or postponed in recent weeks following attacks on the country by the Houthis in Yemen. The US is one of 48 teams scheduled to play in the Under-17 World Cup, in a group with Montenegro, Chile and Algeria. The Under-17 World Cup shifted to an annual event last year, and is being held in Qatar for five consecutive years. Announcing its host decision in 2024, FIFA said the decision to choose a single host nation for multiple editions centered on the ability to make “use of existing footballing infrastructure in the interest of tournament efficiencies and sustainability”. nigeria.description: An art project that started as a final-year assessment at Auchi Polytechnic, Auchi, Edo State, Nigeria, has turned into a full-time career for Konboye Eugene. In his studio in Kuto, Abeokuta, Ogun State, the Nigerian artist is giving discarded footwear a new lease of life, transforming them into colourful portraits. “I’ve been a full-time studio practitioner for about seven years now. I started when I was in my final year at Auchi Polytechnic, where I studied painting,” Eugene said. “It started as an assignment for me when I was in school. But over the course of my practice, I have become a bit more environmentally aware.” ﻿ Statistics cited by Green Network Asia indicate that over 200 million pairs of flip-flops are discarded each year globally, contributing significantly to plastic and rubber pollution in landfills and oceans. Materials ‘Everywhere, Anywhere’ Eugene’s craft draws attention to the environmental impact of discarded footwear and the need for better ways to manage waste. “I source my material through landfills, the streets, literally everywhere, anywhere,” he added. This image shows Eugene assessing discarded footwear he used for his artwork. (Photo: ChannelsTV/Kenny Akinwunmi) The artist shares the detailed process of how he brings each work of art to life. “My process entails getting the materials first, after which we wash them. After we wash them, we have to select and separate them according to their colours, tones, and values.” “I work in two different ways. There’s the assemblage part, where I assemble the footwear. And there’s also the tapestry, where I have to break them into tiny circles and fix them together using copper and aluminium wire,” Eugene explained. Statistics cited by Green Network Asia indicate that over 200 million pairs of flip-flops are discarded each year globally, contributing significantly to plastic and rubber pollution in landfills and oceans. Creating each piece of artwork comes with its challenges, as Eugene says the process can take between two and six months, depending on its size and complexity. “There are a whole lot of challenges that come with the work. There are times when we’re working and have creative blockages. And also, because we work with sharp objects like knives, needles, and all that, there’s also the hazard that comes with it. “I think we work between two to six months, depending on the size and complexity of what we’re working on in the studio,” he said. For Eugene, the message goes beyond the finished artwork, as he hopes his work will change how people perceive and handle discarded materials. “These are materials that are known to be non-biodegradable, meaning all the footwear that I’ve used over the course of the years, they’re all out there. business.title: MSCI Removes Strategy (MSTR) From Its USA Index, Forcing Index Funds to Sell by Nov. 30
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine MSCI Removes Strategy (MSTR) From Its USA Index, Forcing Index Funds to Sell by Nov. 30 MSCI will remove Strategy, the largest corporate bitcoin holder, from the MSCI USA Index as of the close of Nov. 30, the index provider said Wednesday, after a new screen classified the company as a non-operating issuer. The decision is part of MSCI’s November 2026 Index Review , posted shortly after 5 p.m. ET. Official additions and deletions lists show Strategy (MSTR) out of its USA Index, which also takes it out of the broader MSCI World and ACWI indexes. The same review deletes Japan’s Metaplanet from the MSCI Japan Small Cap Index and uranium holder Yellow Cake from the MSCI United Kingdom Small Cap Index, and it removes Iceland’s Skel Fjárfestingafélag from the MSCI Iceland Frontier Markets Small Cap Index and micro-cap Upexi from the USA Micro Cap Index. All five had already been marked Deleted on MSCI’s potential-impact list , built on Sept. 30 financial data and Oct. 9 market values. Strategy is the only large-cap name in the group and, on that October list, accounted for more than 90% of the five companies’ combined float-adjusted market value. The company held 850,364 bitcoin as of Nov. 8, acquired at an average price of $75,456 a coin, or $64.16 billion in aggregate. Strategy shares closed at $122.35, up 1.06%, then slipped 1.51% to $120.50 in after-hours trading as of 5:34 p.m. ET. How the MSCI screen works The rule does not mention bitcoin. The index first checks whether a company’s operating assets equal at least 50% of total assets. Issuers that fail that core screen face five financial ratios, and a company flagged on four or more of them is ineligible for the MSCI Global Investable Market Indexes. Buffers limit turnover. A company outside the indexes cannot be added if it fails the ineligibility screen in either of its two most recent annual filing periods, but a current constituent is removed only if it fails in each of them. The index said it may also use the most recent interim filing. MSCI also said Wednesday that the same non-operating treatment will apply to the MSCI US Index Series. The screen replaces an approach aimed squarely at crypto. The index first proposed in late 2025 to exclude companies whose digital assets made up 50% or more of total assets, then dropped that plan in January and opened a broader consultation in August. It adopted the new methodology on Oct. 15, with minor modifications, and said it would end the interim measures it had placed on those companies in October 2025, including a freeze on share-count increases and a deferral of additions. What the deletion does and does not do Funds that track an MSCI index have to hold what the index holds, so they will have to sell the deleted stocks by the Nov. 30 close. entertainment.title: What Are The Effective Ways of Using AI?
entertainment.description: Two people engaging with technology in a contemporary hotel lobby work setting. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing how people learn, work, communicate and solve problems. In today’s world, if you’re not on board with AI, it could be said you’re being resistant to the fastest-growing technological innovation in the world. From students researching academic subjects to professionals developing business ideas, AI tools have become companions in everyday activities for people. They can help save time, explore new ideas, understand difficult concepts and approach tasks differently. However, as more people embrace these AI tools, it is important to understand that using AI effectively goes beyond knowing what prompts to enter. It requires knowing when to use it, how to question its responses and, most importantly, when to rely on your own knowledge and judgement. AI could make us better at what we do, not make us dependent on it. Here are ways we think you use AI effectively: Use AI as a Research Assistant One of the most effective ways to use AI is for research and information gathering. Whether you are writing an article, preparing a presentation or exploring an unfamiliar subject, AI can help you identify relevant topics, explain complex ideas and suggest areas worth investigating. You can ask it to break down unfamiliar concepts, identify key questions, or suggest research directions. However, do not treat every response as fact. Verify important information using credible sources, published research, books and reliable websites. AI can help you find information, but you are responsible for establishing what is true. Use AI to Brainstorm and Explore Ideas Like knowledge gathering, AI can brainstorm ideas with you. Sometimes, the hardest part of starting a project is knowing where to begin. AI can help you overcome this challenge by suggesting ideas, exploring different approaches and presenting perspectives you may not have considered. For writers, entrepreneurs, researchers and creatives, it can be a useful brainstorming partner. You can share an idea, ask questions about its strengths and weaknesses, and explore ways to develop it. However, brainstorming should not become an excuse to surrender your imagination. Let AI expand your thinking, not replace it. Use AI to Improve Your Work, Not Replace Your Skills This is becoming more important. AI can help you identify grammatical errors, improve sentence construction, organise information, summarise lengthy documents and make your communication clearer. sports.description: Dawn Sullivan’s 2027 recruiting class features a nationally recognized setter, an accomplished defensive specialist and a St. Louis middle blocker. The group addresses three different positions for Sullivan’s program, with Fasavalu expected to help direct the offense, Lewis strengthening the back row and Steiner providing another option at the net. Fasavalu, a 5-foot-8 setter from Sierra Canyon High School in California, arrives in Columbia with an extensive list of individual accomplishments. She was named a MaxPreps First Team All-American in 2025 and earned recognition on the organization’s National Player of the Year watchlist. Fasavalu recently reached another milestone, recording her 2,000th career assist during Sierra Canyon’s postseason run. The Trailblazers advanced to the CIF Southern Section Division I championship match Nov. 7, finishing as runner-up to Mater Dei. Lewis, a 5-foot-5 defensive specialist from Lake Norman Charter in North Carolina, joins the Tigers after winning back-to-back state championships. The libero was named the most valuable player of North Carolina’s 4A state competition during the latest championship run. She also earned Charlotte-area Player of the Year recognition from the Charlotte Observer and played club volleyball with Carolina Union. Lewis served as a team captain at Lake Norman Charter, which finished the 2026 season with a 30-1 record. Steiner gives Missouri another in-state addition. The 6-foot-5 middle blocker from Lindbergh High School in St. Louis has experience competing with USA Volleyball’s national development programs and was selected to the U19 National Team roster. She also played club volleyball with High Performance STL. Steiner earned First Team All-State recognition in Missouri in 2025 and was named to the JVA All-National Team in each of the past two seasons. The three signings give Sullivan another recruiting group as Missouri continues building its roster for the future. With a setter who has surpassed 2,000 career assists, a defensive specialist with championship experience and a 6-foot-5 middle blocker, the Tigers bring in players with different skill sets and competitive backgrounds. Oregon Ducks coach Dan Lanning took a slight shot at Michigan for how the football program has distributed its money. This came in response to comments about the Ducks' financial advantages in recruiting and roster building. The exchange began when Michigan Wolverines coach Kyle Whittingham suggested Oregon's reported $50 million budget gave the program a significant advantage in the increasingly competitive NIL landscape. Whittingham praised Lanning for his work, but also acknowledged the resources available to Oregon, mostly tied to Nike. "It doesn't hurt that you have $50-plus million dollars at your disposal to, in essence, outbid everybody,' Whittingham said. "Not everybody, but a lot of people." Lanning took issue with the basis of the comment. He responded by talking about Michigan's financial commitments, particularly money still owed to departing coaches. "They're spending more of their money right now on their coaches that they're letting go, so maybe it makes it hard to sign players,'" Lanning said. He also suggested Michigan had secured players Oregon could not match financially. "I know they've signed a couple of guys that we weren't able to compete with what they decided to do,' Lanning said. "Maybe a lot of that money is tied up for them in another player." sports.title: Jacob Misiorowski wins unanimous NL Cy Young Award; Cam Schlittler claims AL honors
sports.description: ST PETERSBURG, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 28: Jacob Misiorowski #32 of the Milwaukee Brewers reacts during the fifth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game five of the 2026 World Series at Tropicana Field on October 28, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the third year in a row, the Cy Young race was somewhat of a foregone conclusion. Today, Brewers right-hander Jacob Misiorowski was named the unanimous National League Cy Young Award winner, joining Randy Johnson (2001) and Justin Verlander (2022) as the only pitchers since 2000 to win the Cy Young and the World Series in the same year. He is the fourth Brewer to win the award in franchise history, following Rollie Fingers (1981), Pete Vuckovich (1982), and Corbin Burnes (2021). Misiorowski flashed as a rookie last year, starting off hot and (controversially) making the All-Star team after just five career starts, but he struggled with his command down the stretch and finished the year with a 4.36 ERA. This year, in his first full season as a big-leaguer, Misiorowski worked out the kinks and became completely and utterly dominant, leading the majors in ERA (1.80), strikeouts (252), and WHIP (0.80) while going 16-5. Highlights from his record-breaking season include: Making history with the first-ever 15-strikeout “Maddux” (a complete-game shutout on fewer than 100 pitches) in an early-June game against the Phillies. Misiorowski was a Kyle Schwarber single away from a perfect game, and his 15 strikeouts tied Corbin Burnes for the second-most in a game in Brewers history, behind only Ben Sheets (18). Setting the record for the fastest pitch ever thrown by a starting pitcher, a 105.5-mph fastball. Throwing 1,115 pitches at 100 mph or harder, the most in a season since tracking began in 2008, shattering Jordan Hicks’ previous record of 673 in 2018. Making the National League All-Star team for the second time in as many years. Holding opponents to a .157 batting average, the lowest on record for a full season. Becoming the first Brewer in history to lead the league in both ERA and strikeouts in the same season. Starting the game that clinched the first World Series title in franchise history. Cristopher Sánchez of the Phillies finished second for the second year in a row, receiving 17 of 30 second-place votes, while Braves left-hander Chris Sale finished third. In the American League, fellow second-year starter Cam Schlittler also won the award unanimously. Schlittler put together an amazing season of his own, leading AL starters in WAR (7.0), ERA (1.95), and ERA+ (215). Dylan Cease of the Blue Jays finished second, and rookie Parker Messick of the Guardians finished third.

sports.description: MIAMI, FLORIDA - APRIL 17: Eduardo Rodriguez #57 of the Arizona Diamondbacks looks on following the first inning against the Miami Marlins at loanDepot park on April 17, 2025 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images Unsurprisingly, Jacob Misiorowski was the winner of the NL Cy Young award, getting all thirty first-place votes. But there was some love for Arizona further down the ballot, with Eduardo Rodriguez getting two fifth-place votes, from Tyler Kepner of the Athletic, and Dejan Kovacevic of DK Pittsburgh Sports. E-Rod is the first D-back to be mentioned since 2023, and the first apart from Zac Gallen since 2018. His ERA of 2.89 was fifth among qualified pitchers in the National League, and by wins (16), he only trailed Cristopher Sánchez of the Phillies (18). It’s hard to believe, but half of the 2026 NFL season is in the books. Time flies! This season has brought some pleasant surprises, like the Browns and the Giants, and also some extreme disappointments (hello, Chargers). With nine weeks in the books and nine still left to go, it’s time to check in once again on the NFL awards races. The MVP race is still wide open, with five realistic candidates and a lot of new faces. Lamar Jackson, unfortunately, was taken out of the MVP running by injuries. The Offensive Player of the Year race is also razor-thin, with different players around the league carrying their offenses in different ways. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) There are so many different ways that these races can go over the next nine weeks. Let’s check in with where they are now, how far they’ve come over the last month, and who to look out for during the second half of the season. NFL MVP: Packers QB Jordan Love Eric Canha-Imagn Images Quarter-season pick: Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker Honorable mention: Bengals QB Joe Burrow, Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence, 49ers QB Brock Purdy, Bills QB Josh Allen All five of these guys are all worthy candidates for the award, and all five might win it in a normal year. But all of them have been on fire this season and are leading some of the best offenses in the NFL, making this a very tough race to call. Burrow is playing the best football of his career, Lawrence is a hyper-efficient supercomputer on the most dominant team in football, Purdy is orchestrating the best offense in the league, and Allen is still the most unstoppable force in the NFL. But Love gets the nod here for the amount of weight he has to carry in order for this Packers offense to run the way it does. Green Bay’s offensive line is below average at best, especially after all of the injuries it has suffered. The running game is historically bad and ranks 32nd in the NFL in just about every relevant stat you will find. Despite that, Love has this passing game absolutely humming, and the Packers have won five of their last six games as a result. Through nine weeks, Love leads the league in passing yards and is third in passing touchdowns. sports.title: Youngest pair of Cy Young winners in 41 years shows future of pitching has arrived
sports.description: They embraced the modern ethos of pitching from the moment they turned professional. And now Jacob Misiorowski and Cam Schlittler have proven the future of pitching has arrived. Misiorowski, 24, and Schlittler, 25, won the National and American league Cy Young Awards , respectively, in balloting announced on Nov. 11. And in doing so, they made a certain kind of history: They are the youngest Cy Young-winning duo since 1985, when 20-year-old Dwight Gooden and 21-year-old Bret Saberhagen took home NL and AL honors. Gooden and Saberhagen went on to excellent, World Series-winning careers, even if they could not sustain that level of dominance when they were barely or not quite old enough to legally drink. And their victories didn’t necessarily portend a changing of the guard in the pitching pantheon. Yet, The Miz and Schlitt seemed to prove a point in making 30 and 33 starts and consistently pitching deep into games for the Milwaukee Brewers and New York Yankees , respectively: Yes, significant gains in velocity can be taught – and throwing as hard as you can as long as you can, at least for one season, is sustainable. Schlittler’s fastball barely hit 88 mph coming out of Northeastern as a seventh-round pick in 2022. Misiorowski was in that same range when Brewers scouts pondered drafting him out of high school. Yet both young men matured physically. Schlittler now packs 215 pounds on his 6-foot-6 frame, while Misiorowski is still a relative drink of water at 6-7, 201 – but seemingly growing every day. Perhaps more important, they got drafted by clubs that were fantastic fits. Schlittler’s mechanics and repertoire were remade under a pitching department led by Sam Briend, a former Driveline director of pitching and now the senior voice among Yankee pitching staffers. One of Briend’s first hires, Preston Claiborne, came up the ladder with Schlittler and is now assistant pitching coach for the major league club. Meanwhile, Misiorowski has exceeded the hopes Brewers scouts held when they projected he’d eventually top 100 mph. Try 105 mph. The Miz threw 28 of the 35 hardest pitches in the major leagues this season, ranging from 104 to 105.5 mph. That’s great eye candy, but the numbers at the end of September are even better: 252 strikeouts with a 1.80 ERA, two of the seven major statistical categories in which Misiorowski led the major leagues. Schlittler won his own ERA title, posting a 1.95 mark to lead the AL. And he pitched 193 2/3 innings, just shy of the 200-inning plateau that was once the bare minimum of quality production, yet just three pitchers exceeded this season. Still, for Schlittler to reach that mark in his first full season is an excellent sign he might yet resemble what we all considered an ace. sports.title: Mount Olive volleyball tops North Hunterdon, advances to Group final
sports.description: MOUNT OLIVE — Ava Diaz held the NJSIAA Group 3 North volleyball trophy tightly, with both arms. Amidst the chaotic back gym, the Mount Olive senior libero looked back on the season – and a chance to make history. The Marauders held off North Hunterdon, 25-18, 25-23, 25-23, to clinch the sectional title and extend a confusing and challenging season. Diaz played libero for Mount Olive for the first time, just her second year at the defensive spot. But the big change impacted outside hitters Izabella Osoria and Olivia Drucks. Instead of just stepping up at the net, both became setters – usually to each other. What head coach "modified 6-2" was the brainchild of assistant coach Lee Clowers back in preseason. It took a little while to adjust – noted in the Marauders' lone loss at Randolph on Sept. 9 – but it's become their not-so-secret weapon. Mount Olive won the NJAC-American for the third straight year, knocked off Randolph in the Morris County Tournament final, and now will make its first trip to the Group final since 2016. The Marauders will play Group 3 South champion Toms River South at 1 p.m. Nov. 14 at Franklin High School. Flashback! Mount Olive's big hitters pave path to MCT volleyball title "This was my final time to prove how good of a team we are," said Diaz, who had 33 digs, a kill, two assists and two aces. "This team, specifically, we have a ton of fire in us. We're all like a family. That's what drives us." With her grandmother, parents, and aunt Elizabeth Vega from Orlando, Florida, watching from the front row of the bleachers, Osoria had 16 kills, 14 digs, 22 assists and an ace in the sectional final. Misiorowski becomes the fourth Brewers pitcher to win the award, joining Rollie Fingers (1981), Pete Vuckovich (1982) and Corbin Burnes (2021). And of all those seasons, Misiorowski’s is indisputably tops. Misiorowski led all of baseball with a 1.80 earned run average and 252 strikeouts, posting a 16-5 record across 174 ⅔ innings. The sixth-youngest pitcher to win the award, the 24-year-old Misiorowski ran away from the competition over the final four months of the season. More: Pat Murphy wins unprecedented third straight NL manager of the year award Misiorowski, fueled by a strong postseason to finish his rookie year, entered the 2026 season stronger thanks to off-season training that added 20 pounds and focused on his lower half. The results in his improved control were immediately noticeable. technology.title: US bit barn boom sees energy needs grow 10x as fast as grid capacity
technology.description: Datacenter power consumption in the US is growing roughly ten times faster than grid capacity, meaning facilities may soon need to find a large chunk of their own electricity from other sources. Surging demand for AI infrastructure is driving a wave of new server farms across America, but it is exposing long-term underinvestment in the grid networks required to deliver power where it's needed. Insurance broker Howden calculates that datacenters would need to source up to 58 percent of their power off the grid by 2030 just to keep their share of grid capacity from growing. Gartner warned in June that the energy consumed by AI datacenters is on track to grow 26 percent this year, and grid supply may be unable to keep pace with demand by the end of this decade. Howden's analysis of data from the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) and S&P Global found that since the year 2000, power being fed to data campuses has risen 19 percent a year on average, while the electricity grid expanded capacity by just 2 percent per annum over the same period. Datacenters' share of US grid capacity was circa five percent in 2025, up from 0.1 percent in 2000 – a 50-fold increase. Management consultancy Bain & Company issued a report two years ago warning that energy companies must switch gear and invest in building out grid capacity faster , as energy draw by server farms is expected to more than double by 2030. This doesn't mean that datacenters are in danger of eating all of America's electricity, at least not in the immediate future. The graph makes it appear that the two lines are about to cross, but the chart uses different scales: 1,400 gigawatts on the left axis for grid capacity, versus just 80 on the right for datacenters. Keeping datacenters at five percent of grid capacity requires 110 gigawatts of behind-the-meter capacity by 2030, Howden estimates – an expansion it considers unlikely. Instead, it expects a combination of greater reliance on the grid, slower development at power-constrained sites, and alternative supplies. For the largest, most power-constrained projects, Howden warns that grid delays of two to six years could mean $800 million to $2.4 billion in forgone revenue. "Power availability is becoming one of the defining challenges of the datacenter boom," says Howden head of Natural Resources Stuart Adam. "As demand for AI infrastructure accelerates, developers are increasingly looking beyond traditional grid connections to secure the electricity they need." Howden's business is insurance, and so Adam also notes that on-site generation introduces new operational and financial exposures, as operators take greater responsibility for their power infrastructure. ®

science.description: The River Wye in Derbyshire, England Dave Porter/Alamy The concentration of two of the most well-studied PFAS forever chemicals are showing a strong downward trend in English rivers. The finding adds to a mixed story for the power of global restrictions. The levels of perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) in English rivers have fallen by 30 per cent and 29 per cent, respectively, over the past decade, according to a new report by scientists at the Environment Agency (EA) , a UK government green regulator. Both of these human-made chemicals take a long time to break down in the environment. The International Agency for Research on Cancer recently designated PFOA as carcinogenic to humans , and both forever chemicals have been linked to reproductive health and developmental impacts as well as other serious health issues. They had both been used in non-stick coatings on consumer products as well as in industrial processes. Both were also used in firefighting foams, a major source of PFAS pollution entering the environment, with a ban on PFOA in firefighting foams only coming into force in the UK in 2025. The plan is to establish a fresh NASA strategy for gathering Mars samples collected by the Perseverance rover and launching them back to Earth. science.title: We can't see Fast Radio Bursts but we can now hear them thanks to a Finnish Cathedral
science.description:
Sharmila Kuthunur is an independent space journalist based in Bengaluru, India. Her work has also appeared in Scientific American, Science, Astronomy and Live Science, among other publications. She holds a master's degree in journalism from Northeastern University in Boston. 

Fast radio bursts, flashes of energy from faraway galaxies, are invisible to our eyes. However, we can now hear their melody, thanks to a composer who has turned them into sound. Fast radio bursts, or FRBs , are among the most extreme events in the universe, releasing as much energy in a millisecond as the sun puts out in three days and briefly outshining entire galaxies. Since the first FRB was discovered in 2007, astronomers have detected thousands of them; however, exactly how these cosmic flares are launched remains poorly understood. Recent evidence points to at least one burst coming from the environment around a rotating neutron star. Despite their power, FRBs last only a few thousandths of a second before vanishing into space. Catching one takes luck, as a telescope has to be pointed at the right patch of sky at the right moment. That changed with CHIME (the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment) in British Columbia. With a very wide field of view and a supercomputer to process its data, CHIME more than quadrupled the number of known FRBs in its first year of operation alone. Between 2018 and 2023, CHIME recorded 4,539 bursts from 3,641 sources. As pulses of radio waves, our eyes haven't evolved to see FRBs, nor can we hear them as they aren't sound waves. Well, not until now. "Artist and composer Andrew Melchior turned all of the CHIME bursts into sound for "The Logos," an installation that has played daily at Oulu Cathedral in Finland since early April and is scheduled to run through the end of the year. Melchior and Kiyoshi Masui, an associate professor of physics at MIT, "sonified" the bursts, translating data into acoustics so that human ears can hear them. The structure of each real signal is mapped to varying musical pitches and played through 12 loudspeakers spread throughout the cathedral. The result is a range of tones, with distant FRBs humming, rumbling, popping, and whistling. The signals are old by any human measure. According to a description on Melchior's website , the youngest in the work are about 50 million years old, and the oldest are about 8 to 9 billion years old. Saxton, NRAO/AUI/NSF)) Physics also plays a role in what is heard. Each burst arrives with its high frequencies first and sweeps downward, stretched by its journey through intergalactic gas, "and you can hear that dispersion as it falls from the dome," Melchior told Space.com by email. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 11, 1966: NASA launches Gemini 12 mission with astronaut icons Buzz Aldrin and Jim Lovell aboard
science.description: null On Nov. 11, 1966, the Gemini 12 mission launched an astronaut crew into orbit and set the stage for NASA's Apollo program to land humans on the moon. Gemini 12 was the last mission of the Gemini program. It had two astronauts on board: Jim Lovell and Buzz Aldrin . NASA wanted to send humans to the moon. But first, it needed to make sure crews had the right skills, like docking vehicles in space and taking spacewalks. Before Gemini 12, astronauts struggled with spacewalks because there weren't enough handholds on their spacecraft. NASA made some spacewalk changes for Gemini 12. Aldrin performed three spacewalks and spent more than five hours working in space with no major problems. Gemini 12 also successfully docked to an unpiloted Agena booster that launched the same day. The astronauts returned to Earth after four days in space. Both Aldrin and Lovell went on to join the Apollo program . Aldrin became the second person to walk on the moon during Apollo 11 , and Lovell became the commander of Apollo 13 . The Gemini 12 astronauts James Lovell and Edwin Aldrin lifted off aboard a Titan launch vehicle from the Kennedy Space Center on November 11, 1966, an hour and a half after their Agena target vehicle was orbited by an Atlas rocket. (Image credit: NASA/MSFC) Why it mattered Gemini 12 may have closed out NASA's Gemini program of two-person space missions, but it established the mission also established the fundamentals of spacewalking that Apollo astronauts would use when they walked on the moon. It's fitting that Aldrin was the primary spacewalker of the mission. A rookie astronaut (and the first to earn a Ph.D.), Aldrin set a precedent by training for his spacewalk in a neutral buoyancy pool in Maryland to better simulate working in weightlessness. Then he did it again as the second person to walk on the moon on Apollo 11. "This approach became so successful, underwater training has become the primary spacewalk training method used by the United State, Russia and China," NASA officials said in a mission overview . science.description: Coloured X-ray of osteoarthritis of the knee ALAIN POL/SCIENCE PHOTO LIBRARY A drug that prevents blood clots reduced pain and improved mobility in mice and monkeys with knee osteoarthritis. The approach seems to partly work by reducing inflammatory signals that degrade cartilage. Osteoarthritis is caused by the wear and tear of cartilage that cushions the ends of bones, leading to inflammation, pain and stiffness. It affects more than 500 million people worldwide. Painkillers and anti-inflammatory drugs can relieve symptoms, but no approved drugs halt or slow worsening of the disease. “We have nothing to offer our patients apart from suggesting weight loss, or offering drugs that provide pain relief,” says Tonia Vincent at the University of Oxford, who wasn’t involved in the study. Advertisement Read more The best non-drug therapies to relieve the pain of knee osteoarthritis It is widely thought that inflammatory molecules called TNF-alpha and IL-1-beta drive inflammation that worsens osteoarthritis. This has led to clinical trials testing drugs that target either of these molecules. But these have been unsuccessful, potentially because these molecules compensate for each other when one is blocked, according to Chuan-Ju Liu at Yale University and his colleagues. To explore whether targeting both molecules may be more effective, the researchers surgically removed part of the cartilage in the left knee joints of eight monkeys to mimic wear and tear that triggers osteoarthritis. A month later, four of the monkeys took a daily dose of a drug called dabigatran, mixed into their food. Dabigatran is commonly used to prevent blood clots in people at increased risk of strokes, but has also been shown to block inflammatory signals via both TNF-alpha and IL-1-beta. The remaining monkeys ate their usual food as a control. This suggests that the drug reduced cartilage damage, slowing the progression of osteoarthritis, says Liu. science.title: Andy Weir's 'Exoplanet' just landed on Audible, but what actually makes an exoplanet habitable?
science.description: null Imagine you’ve crash-landed on an alien planet. Your ship is destroyed, your oxygen supply is dangerously low, and the landscape around you is completely unknown. Where would you begin looking for clues to your survival? Surprisingly, the best place to start could be the star overhead. This is the predicament that three crew members of the Wild Blue Yonder face in Audible’s new sci-fi thriller, "Exoplanet." This sci-fi thriller is written by acclaimed comic writer Benjamin Percy, executive produced by Andy Weir (Project Hail Mary, The Martian), and features an all-star voice cast including Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo . Stranded on an unfamiliar planet, they encounter volcanic wastelands, unknown skies, and environments that seem to defy reason. But behind the extraordinary events of this audio drama is a very real scientific question: what makes a planet habitable? Learning from the stars An artist's concept illustrates a young, red dwarf star surrounded by three planets. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) In “Exoplanet”, the crew view skies that are not only unfamiliar but also seemingly different from one another. One character sees a sun as so dim that he can look directly at it, while another suffers under a blazing heat, surrounded by stretches of sun-scorched red rock. For astronomers, the light emitted by a star is one of the most crucial tools for understanding planets orbiting it. Using a technique called spectroscopy , astronomers split starlight into its constituent wavelengths, producing a spectrum much like a rainbow. By studying this spectrum, they can investigate the temperature, composition, and other physical properties of the star. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) However, stellar temperature is only part of the picture. The amount of energy a planet receives depends on both the luminosity of the star and its orbital distance. Astronomers use these measurements to determine whether a world lies in the habitable zone of a star, where temperatures could allow liquid water to exist on the surface given a suitable atmosphere. A planet orbiting a cool red dwarf would need to be much closer to its star than Earth is to the Sun to be in this habitable zone. Unfortunately, being in this zone is no guarantee of a planetary paradise. Hostile stars Black holes are bad news for life, but living stars provide just as many problems. (Image credit: Audible) A planet that sits comfortably in the habitable zone is ultimately still at the mercy of its star. Stars emit more than just the light we see. Ultraviolet radiation and X-rays can interact with planetary atmospheres, altering chemistry and even contributing to the loss of the atmosphere . Violent stellar flares can produce bursts of high-energy radiation. A planet could offer a wonderfully balmy temperature, only to be bombarded with radiation from the host star. science.title: Who will step up to preserve space age artefacts for future generations?
science.description: NASA/JPL-Caltech Around 40,000 years from now, the Voyager 1 probe will pass within astronomical spitting distance of the star Gliese 445. From there, it will continue drifting through the universe on an endless journey that marks humanity’s first attempt to reach the stars. Voyager 1 – which on 18 November will have travelled one light day from Earth – began its odyssey almost 50 years ago, meaning it has been operating for the majority of the space age. That makes it a rarity: most of our iconic spacecraft ended their lives burned up in Earth’s atmosphere or in bits at the bottom of the ocean. Two of the most important missions still flying today, the Hubble Space Telescope and the International Space Station, look set to share the same fate in the near future, even as scientists call for Hubble to be preserved . While some craft like the space shuttles are on display in museums, our present space history is, essentially, in its dark ages, with little thought currently given to preserving spacecraft in situ, where our space-travelling descendants may wish to marvel at them. Even the Apollo hardware left behind on the moon has almost no protection in international law. Advertisement Perhaps we need an organisation like the UNESCO World Heritage Committee to designate important space artefacts for preservation, and encourage funding from cultural and heritage budgets, not scientific ones, to do this. Of course, with such budgets often under threat and the US set to leave UNESCO at the end of this year, this could introduce new problems. Private philanthropy is another option. If humanity is to one day take its place among the stars, a fantasy that fuels many a tech billionaire, it would be a great shame to not be able to look back at how we got there. Just as we remember 19th-century captains of industry like Andrew Carnegie and J. P. Morgan for funding great cultural institutions, perhaps we should be lobbying for the creation of a Musk Space Museum or Bezos Orbital Institute.

Shot by Roger Patterson and Robert Gimlin in 1967, the clip became one of the canonical pieces of evidence for the existence of Bigfoot: a mythical humanoid that supposedly lives in the forests of North America. Bigfoot is one of the icons of cryptozoology, the search for probably-nonexistent creatures. It has hordes of devotees. In Capturing Bigfoot , film-maker Marq Evans uncovers what really happened in 1967. He speaks to Patterson’s associate Bob Heironimus, who says he wore an ape costume in the footage. science.title: Did comets bring building blocks of life to Earth? Scientists aren't so sure anymore
science.description: The origin of life on Earth remains a mystery. New research shows that comets almost certainly did not bring the chemical building blocks of life to our planet. Life as we know it is based around carbon chemistry, also known as organic chemistry. Complex organic molecules are the fundamental building blocks of biochemical compounds such as nucleobases, amino acids, sugars and so on that act as the machinery for biochemistry on Earth . Two big questions are where did this complex chemistry originate? Did these complex organic molecules form on Earth, or were they delivered here from space? New research led by planetary scientist Richard Anslow of the Institute for Astronomy at the University of Cambridge has now seemingly ruled out comets as the origin of complex organic molecules on Earth. "Historically, scientists thought that comets were important for the origin of life on Earth, because they carried carbon and nitrogen-bearing molecules, so these giant space snowballs were almost like a 'get-out-of-jail-free card' that brought all the molecules a planet would need to seed life," said Anslow in a statement . Stripping the romance from the Earth's turbulent past Comet impacts on Earth were much more frequent in the first half-billion years of the solar system ’s existence, when there were still lots of debris leftover from the formation of the planets. For over a century comet impacts had been considered a prime suspect in the search for what brought the building blocks of life to Earth. However, while comets bringing the building blocks of life to Earth is "kind of a romantic idea," according to Anslow, the University of Cambridge researcher added that the team's results suggest that is highly unlikely. Anslow and colleagues arrived at this conclusion based upon computer modeling by using the very latest simulations depicting the origin and evolution of comets and their orbits, their interactions with Earth's atmosphere as they enter it, and of the hypervelocity comet impacts themselves. In particular, they used the fate of hydrogen cyanide as a proxy for what happens to complex organic molecules in comet impacts. Hydrogen cyanide is frequently found in comets and was even detected in the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS . An artist’s impression of a comet crashing into the early Earth (Image credit: Scarlett White) The problem is that comets are generally moving at too great a velocity. For organic molecules to survive impact, the impact velocity would have to be below 33,500 miles per hour (15 kilometers per second). Anslow and his colleagues found that, in general, comets travel too fast and enter Earth’s atmosphere at too sharp an angle for complex organic molecules to survive. Instead, they are mostly vaporized on impact. Even on the rare occasions that the complex organic molecules survived, they were usually not in great enough abundance to provide any meaningful prebiotic chemistry.
